description: DFT relaxed V0 coordinates, PBC distance calculation

modelc_v3._note: Li-Cl split by Cl site: 4a (n=36) vs 4d anti-site (n=4). 4d-Cl 0.19 A shorter.

bader_charges_PAW_AE_plot_num_17._method: Henkelman bader v1.05 on QE pp.x plot_num=17 AE charge density. PAW kjpaw_psl 1.0.0 pseudo, same SCF as LOBSTER ext basis (ecutwfc=70 Ry). Convention: q_atom = N_valence_electron - N_bader_basin.

S._note: high σ because of PS4-S vs 4d-S²⁻ environment split

P._note: large σ from 4d-Cl anti-site distorting PS4 basin shape

wilkening_ionic_potential_eV_A._formula: |q(Li) × q(X)| / d(Li-X) — proxy for cation-anion Coulomb attraction (Wilkening 2019, Zhang 2024)

delta_LPSCl_to_LPSCl16.Li-S: +16.8% (stronger ionic glue from S-charge increase + slightly shorter Li-S)
delta_LPSCl_to_LPSCl16.Li-Cl: +1.1% (~unchanged — vacancy effect cancels with anti-site shift)
delta_LPSCl_to_LPSCl16.interpretation: Li-S ionic potential dominates in BOTH systems. LPSCl1.6 boost is concentrated in Li-S; Li-Cl is barely affected by composition. Consistent with ICOHP showing all bonds stronger in LPSCl1.6, with Bader pinpointing the Li-S channel as primary contributor.

icohp_distance_correlation_eV_per_Angstr._method: Per-bond ICOHP from LOBSTER ICOHPLIST.lobster (ext basis) regressed vs bond distance d (Å). Slope dICOHP/dd (eV/Å) measures bond stiffness: large slope = covalent (length-sensitive), small slope = ionic (length-flat).

Cl-Li(4a)._note: Linear in d; ICOHP σ = d_σ × slope = 0.129 × 4.94 ≈ 0.638

Li-S(4d)._note: Steeper than Li-Cl due to S²⁻ deeper potential

P-S._note: Similar to comp1 — PS4 backbone robust

Cl-Li(4a)._note: 2.3× FLATTER than comp1 4a — ionic softening from Cl-rich field

icohp_distance_correlation_eV_per_Angstr.interpretation: LPSCl1.6 ionic bonds (Li-Cl, Li-S) have 2-3× flatter ICOHP-distance slopes than LPSCl. Flatter slope = bond becomes less sensitive to length variation = more ionic character = lower vibrational stiffness. This is a QUANTITATIVE measure of why finite-T motion is easier in LPSCl1.6 (relevant to AIMD higher D). PS4 covalent backbone slope unchanged (+11-12 eV/Å) — PS4 robust to composition. Independent confirmation of the 'ionic-glue strengthening + bond softening' duality observed in static ICOHP averages.

wilkening_ICOHP_3way_correlation._method: Per-bond Bader-derived Wilkening ionic potential |q_Li × q_X|/d vs LOBSTER ICOHP regression. Tests whether the ionic potential framework (Wilkening 2019, Zhang 2024) predicts LOBSTER ICOHP at the single-bond level.
wilkening_ICOHP_3way_correlation._key_finding: Wilkening potential PERFECTLY predicts Li-Cl ICOHP: r=-1.000 (comp1) and r=-0.988 (modelc). Single-metric (Bader q) and single-metric (distance) combination directly reproduces a fundamentally different method (LOBSTER projected COHP). Strongest single quantitative validation of the ionic potential framework for argyrodites.

Li-S(4d)._note: Anomalous +slope is artifact of very narrow range (d=2.35-2.38, ICOHP=-2.43 to -2.69)

Li-S(PS4)._note: Weaker correlation due to wide d range incorporating very long bonds at edge of cutoff

Cl-Li(4a)._note: Excellent Wilkening prediction; 1.6× gentler slope than comp1 = softer bonds

Li-S(PS4)._note: Stronger correlation than comp1 — Li-S(PS4) more consistently ionic in vacancy structure

wilkening_ICOHP_3way_correlation.paper_message: The Wilkening ionic potential is the underlying physics. LOBSTER ICOHP, Bader charges, and bond distances are not independent descriptors — they are three projections of the same Coulombic attraction. This explains why all three metrics shift in the same direction between LPSCl and LPSCl1.6 (all stronger ionic in LPSCl1.6).

strongest_bonds_per_system_top5._method: Per-bond ICOHP ranked (most negative first), top 5 per system
strongest_bonds_per_system_top5._note: Top 5 in both systems are all P-S covalent backbone bonds, ~-6.4 eV at d≈2.04 Å — textbook argyrodite PS4³⁻ signature.

bader_q_vs_n_Cl_correlation_modelc_v3._method: Li Bader charge grouped by number of Cl neighbors within 3.4 Å cutoff
bader_q_vs_n_Cl_correlation_modelc_v3.interpretation: Each Cl neighbor adds approximately +0.011 e to Li Bader charge — linear, predictable. Li ionicity is composition-tunable via anion environment. Combined with the ICOHP-distance slope finding, this gives two independent metrics for the 'Cl-rich field strengthens Li ionicity' effect.

icohp_LOBSTER_ext_basis_eV_per_bond._method: LOBSTER 5.1.1, PAW kjpaw_psl 1.0.0 pseudo, ecutwfc=70 Ry, NSCF nbnd 450 (comp1) / 500 (modelc_v3), wf_collect, nosym. Extended basis: Li 1s 2s 2p, P/S/Cl 3s 3p 3d. Charge spilling < 1.5% for both. Paper-grade absolute values.
icohp_LOBSTER_ext_basis_eV_per_bond._convention: ICOHP < 0 = bonding. Per-bond average over all bonds within 4.0 Å cutoff (cohpGenerator).

Li-S(4d)._note: Free S²⁻ at 4d; universal anchor (≈ same in modelc_v3)

Li_S_per_site_split.headline: Same Li-S(4d) ICOHP as modelc_v3 (-2.57 vs -2.52, <2% difference) → 4d S²⁻ universal Li anchor confirmed independent of composition.

Li-Cl(4a)._note: Normal 4a octahedral Cl[Li6→Li5 with vacancy]; large σ from Li-vacancy environment heterogeneity

Li-Cl(4d)._note: Anti-site tet Cl[Li4]; tight σ from well-defined environment (single Cl, 4 Li neighbors)

Li_Cl_per_site_split.headline: 4d-Cl anti-site forms 40% stronger Li-Cl bonds than 4a-Cl. Despite being only 12.5% of Cl (1/8), it contributes substantially to mean ICOHP (-2.103 avg vs -2.026 if 4a-only). Direct quantitative origin of the deeper second peak in Li-Cl pCOHP panel.

Li_Cl_vacancy_antisite_decomposition._method: Compare comp1 4a-only ICOHP (no vacancy) with modelc 4a (with vacancy) to isolate vacancy effect, then compare modelc 4a with modelc 4d to isolate anti-site effect.
Li_Cl_vacancy_antisite_decomposition.headline: Vacancy/Cl-rich field is the MAIN driver of Li-Cl strengthening (69% of total), affecting all 90% of Cl atoms uniformly. Anti-site provides INTENSE per-bond enhancement (40% stronger) but on only 10% of Cl, contributing 31% to total. The two effects together explain the +13.4% overall Li-Cl ICOHP increase.

Li-S(PS4)._note: PS4-bound S; ionic glue varies by Li env

Li-S(4d)._note: Free S²⁻ at 4d site; tight σ → universal Li-S anchor

Li_S_per_site_split.headline: Free 4d S²⁻ forms 55% stronger and 13× more uniform Li-S bonds than PS4-bound S. 4d-S²⁻ is a universal Li anchor invariant to composition (cf. comp1 4d-S²⁻ ICOHP = -2.566, only 2% different).

headline_comparison.Li-Cl_delta_pct: +13.4% (LPSCl1.6 stronger; driven by short 4d-Cl Li-Cl bonds and overall Cl-rich ionic field)
headline_comparison.Li-S_delta_pct: +7.9% (LPSCl1.6 stronger; vacancy concentrates remaining Li-S bonds)
headline_comparison.P-S_delta_pct: +0.9% (~unchanged; PS4 backbone robust to Cl substitution)
headline_comparison.paper_message: Vacancy + Cl substitution STRENGTHENS rather than weakens ionic bonding in LPSCl1.6. Wilkening ionic potential framework (q·|q|/r) consistent: shorter Li-Cl(4d) bonds = larger ICOHP magnitude.

trends.Li-Br_vs_Li-Cl: Li-Br 0.10-0.26 A longer in all compositions
trends.P-S_constant: ~2.06 A across all compositions (PS4 framework invariant)
trends.basin_effect: Li-Br differs by 0.012 A between basins (comp5)

physics.longer_bond_weaker: Longer Li-Br -> weaker ionic interaction -> lower B0/E
